_READ_ME: Keys starting with _ are notes, not settings -- the plugin ignores them. Edit the plain keys underneath each note. Run "Unlayered Infill - Check setup" to see these explanations with your own values filled in.
_enabled: Turn the whole plugin off without unselecting it in the preset.
_amplitude: How far the infill rides up and down in Z. A percent ("200%") or a multiple ("2x") is a share of your layer height, so it keeps meaning when you change layer height; a plain number ("-0.2") is millimetres. The sign only shifts the wave along, so it barely matters.
_frequency: Ripples per millimetre. Higher means tighter, more frequent waves. Much above about 3 and neighbouring crests start to merge into each other at normal line spacing.
_segment_mm: Each infill move is chopped into pieces this long to follow the wave. Smaller is smoother and makes a bigger file; much below 0.5 mm mostly buys file size.
_cell_mm: How finely the solid skin above and below is mapped, in millimetres. "auto" uses one column per nozzle width, read from the G-code, which is as fine as the printer can actually resolve.
_blend_mm: Smooth the fade-out across this radius, in millimetres. Where a ledge makes one column's ceiling much lower than its neighbour's, this turns the step between them into a ramp.
_full_strength: Off, the wave peaks at half the amplitude even in the middle of a span. On, it reaches the full amplitude mid-span and still fades to nothing at the skins.
_pattern: "linear" ripples along one direction only. "cross" is an egg-crate that ripples along both, so infill lines running in any direction still rise and fall. With linear, a line that runs ACROSS the ripples gets one constant height for its whole length -- it is lifted, not waved, and keys into nothing. If your infill is 0/90 degrees, or you want interlocking in both directions, use cross.
_wave_angle: Degrees to turn the ripples, counter-clockwise, 0 being along X. Aim them across your infill direction so every line crosses them. With the common 45-degree infill, try 45. Ignored in practice by cross, which already covers both directions.
_shape: "sine" is the smooth classic. "triangle" has straight flanks and sharp peaks, so layers key together harder for the same height. "square" keeps most of the infill at full offset with short ramps between -- it is a saturated sine, never a vertical step, because no printer can move Z instantly.
_layer_phase: Degrees of extra phase added per waved layer. At 0 every layer's crest sits at the same place, leaving a column of crests. A small advance walks the crests sideways as the part grows, which is what actually braids the layers together. 180 puts each crest directly over the trough below it; 360 is a full turn and changes nothing.
_max_lift_mm: A hard ceiling on the Z displacement, in millimetres, whatever the amplitude and taper work out to. 0 means no ceiling. This is a safety net: raise layer height or amplitude without thinking and the nozzle can be driven up into material it has already printed.
_require_relative_e: Refuse to run on absolute-E G-code instead of corrupting it. Leave this on. The fix is Printer Settings > Advanced > Use relative E distances.
_log: Append a readable record of every export to the log file named by Check setup.
